slide_title: Linear and Unit Step Activation Functions

bullets: F(x) = Uni-polar Unit Step = { 0 for x<0 ; 1 for x ≥ 0 }
F(x) = Bi-polar Unit Step = { -1 for x<0 ; 1 for x ≥ 0 }
equations: F(x) = Uni-polar Unit Step = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{for } x < 0 \\ 1 & \text{for } x \ge 0 \end{cases}
F(x) = Bi-polar Unit Step = \begin{cases} -1 & \text{for } x < 0 \\ 1 & \text{for } x \ge 0 \end{cases}

recreation_brief: 1. Create a new PowerPoint slide with a light gray background (#e6e6e6). 2. Add a centered title at the top: 'Linear and Unit Step Activation Functions' in large bold dark red sans-serif (#c00000). 3. Add a yellow circle in the top-right corner containing the number '17'. 4. In the top-center area, draw a blue-bordered rectangle containing a Cartesian graph: x-axis horizontal, f(x)-axis vertical, with a red diagonal line passing through the origin; label the y-axis 'f(x)' at top and x-axis 'x' at right. 5. In the top-right area, draw a large red X mark. Below it, add a peach-colored box (#ffe6cc) with text: 'F(x) = x' in black, followed by 'Linear (No Activation)' in red italic/bold. 6. In the bottom-left area, draw a blue-bordered rectangle containing a Cartesian graph of a unipolar step function: red line flat at y=0 for x<0, vertical jump at x=0, then flat at positive y for x>0; label axes 'f(x)' and 'x'. 7. In the bottom-right area, draw a blue-bordered rectangle containing a Cartesian graph of a bipolar step function: red line flat at negative y for x<0, vertical jump at x=0, then flat at positive y for x>0; label axes 'f(x)' and 'x'. 8. Below the bottom-left graph, add a peach box with: 'F(x) = Uni-polar Unit Step = {' then '0 for x<0' in green, '1 for x ≥ 0' in green, with a closing brace. 9. Below the bottom-right graph, add a peach box with: 'F(x) = Bi-polar Unit Step = {' then '-1 for x<0' in green, '1 for x ≥ 0' in green, with a closing brace.
